ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act), as amended, together with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2013, and the Companies Act 1993 (ss 87-89, 189 and 193). The AML/CFT Act requires reporting entities to conduct customer due diligence and identify beneficial owners. The New Zealand Companies Register and company share registers are publicly searchable, but true beneficial ownership behind any nominee arrangement is verified by AML/CFT-regulated parties, with statutory access available to the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit, Department of Internal Affairs and Inland Revenue.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Company Registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) issues an Apostille Certificate directly; no consular legalization is required for any state party to the Hague Apostille Convention. Consular Legalization route for non-member states: MFAT first issues an authentication certificate, followed by legalization by the destination state's consular authority in New Zealand; the apostille and consular routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Ongoing Registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For member states of the Apostille Convention: MFAT attaches an Apostille to the Companies Office certificate; no consular stamp is required. For non-member states: MFAT authentication is followed by consular legalization at the receiving country's embassy or consulate accredited to New Zealand. Each path is used alone depending on the destination country.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney for Incorporation and Banking
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding directors and shareholders of the New Zealand limited company (drafted by counsel and notarized by a New Zealand notary public)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private instrument: executed before a New Zealand notary public, then either (a) MFAT Apostille for an Apostille Convention country, or (b) MFAT authentication plus consular legalization for a non-member state. The two authentication paths are alternative, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and directors of the New Zealand company, filed with the New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy confirmed by the New Zealand notary and, where required, MFAT apostille for member states, or MFAT authentication plus consular legalization for non-member states. Both routes remain mutually exclusive; a document that has received an apostille will not additionally be submitted for consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed New Zealand commercial bank such as Bank of New Zealand, ANZ, Westpac, or ASB
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter is confirmed by the bank's authorized signatory and, if required by the receiving regulator, notarized. Authentication is then completed either by MFAT Apostille for Apostille states or by MFAT authentication and consular legalization for non-member states; both routes are alternative and must not be combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening must be conducted on all shareholders, directors, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and any person exercising control over the New Zealand company. Screening must be run against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UK HM Treasury Consolidated Sanctions List where relevant, the New Zealand sanctions designations, and domestic criminal/PEP databases. The AML/CFT Act 2009 requires an explicit politically exposed person (PEP) determination, including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, international organization PEPs, and their family members and close associates. Any positive match triggers enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and, where a suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing arises, a mandatory suspicious transaction report to the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit before the company is formed or used.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Name Availability and Reservation Portal (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz) operated by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin/Roman characters and may include English or te reo Maori words; non-Latin scripts require an approved English or Maori transliteration or translation. The Companies Office applies a four-tier statutory naming convention: (1) availability and distinctiveness against the existing New Zealand company register and trade marks; (2) prohibited and objectionable meaning; (3) misleading or confusion risk under the Companies Act 1993; and (4) advance ministerial/regulator consent for sensitive tokens. A limited liability company name must end with the word Limited or Ltd.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant may, within 10 working days of the rejection notice, request a written statement of reasons and lodge a request for internal administrative review with the New Zealand Companies Office Name Review team. The review request must include the proposed name, proof of trade mark registration or prior use, evidence that the name is not confusingly similar, and submissions explaining why no prohibited token appears. If the internal review is unsuccessful, the applicant may appeal to the District Court, or to the High Court on a question of law under the Companies Act 1993, within 20 working days of the internal review decision. A new reservation may be filed after the statutory stand-down period if the name is released.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office with a genuine physical street address in New Zealand and a staffed service-of-process facility is generally acceptable for company registration and for a low-risk MarTech/SaaS entity. A commercial post-office mailbox alone is not acceptable as a registered office because the Companies Act 1993, section 189, requires a physical address at which legal documents may be served and records kept. Inland Revenue and New Zealand tier-one banks will normally reject a bare letterbox for tax correspondence or bank account opening, especially if the company seeks GST registration or a merchant account with Stripe or Paddle. The safest structure for this industry is to use a licensed registered agent with a real New Zealand street address, mail handling, and director forwarding service, and to maintain evidence of commercial substance such as a physical support address, director location, and customer contracts before requesting high-risk banking approval.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified annual risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection for this low-risk SaaS analytics company is low, approximately 2% to 5%, unless adverse information or a false service-of-process record appears. Checklist: (a) confirm the registered office is a physical New Zealand street address and not a PO Box; (b) confirm there is a person authorized to accept service present during business hours; (c) ensure the company name is visible on any mailbox or reception board if required by the building's lease; (d) keep the Constitution, share register, board resolution, and statutory records at the registered office or lawful alternate location; (e) respond to any request from the Companies Office, Inland Revenue, or local council within five working days; (f) ensure the virtual office contract includes physical inspection acceptance in case the Registrar or tax auditor verifies the site.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), Part 2 (Incorporation) sections 10 through 17; Part 8 (Shares); Part 10 (Directors); Financial Reporting Act 2013; Companies (Fees) Regulations 2018; Tax Administration Act 1994 for post-incorporation tax registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Register), Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company submitted electronically through the New Zealand Companies Register pursuant to section 13 of the Companies Act 1993; approved result is the Certificate of Incorporation and automatic issuance of the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up share capital requirement under the Companies Act 1993. A New Zealand limited company may issue shares for such consideration as the directors determine, commonly NZ$1.00 per ordinary share. There is no statutory blocked escrow account, no capital deposit certificate, and no notarized capital verification requirement for domestic or non-resident-owned shareholders.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: AT A MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF NZ LIMITED (the Company) duly convened and held in accordance with the Company's constitution and the Companies Act 1993, the directors being lawfully present, the following resolutions were moved, seconded, and unanimously adopted. 1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION AND CAPITAL. RESOLVED that the allotment, issue, and subscription of the initial issued ordinary shares of the Company to the subscribers named in the register of shareholders be and is hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved. The directors acknowledge that the Companies Act 1993 imposes no minimum paid-up share capital, and that each share has the rights, preferences, and restrictions set out in the constitution. The directors are authorized to issue additional ordinary shares, to divide or consolidate shares, and to determine the consideration for which those shares are allotted as the Company's funding requirements may require. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at the address for service recorded with the New Zealand Companies Office, and that such office shall be a physical New Zealand address capable of receiving legal documents and statutory notices. The directors, acting through the managing director, are authorized to file all prescribed forms with the Companies Office respecting the registered office and to change the registered office when appropriate in accordance with the Companies Act 1993. 3. STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED that the following persons are hereby appointed as the executive governance team: [Name] as Managing Director, [Name] as Financial Officer or Director, and [Name] as Compliance Officer, each to hold office until removal or resignation in accordance with the constitution. The board confirms that no company secretary is required under New Zealand law, but if a secretary is later proposed, the board may appoint one. The officers are authorized to execute on behalf of the Company any certificates, contracts, consents, applications, and instruments required for the business of providing search engine optimization content analytics tools, data crawler services, and digital marketing software. 4. BANKING AND PAYMENT AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED that the directors are authorized to open, operate, and close bank accounts in the name of the Company, to appoint authorized signatories, and to negotiate and execute agreements with payment providers such as Stripe, Paddle, and other card processors. The officers are authorized to give instructions regarding deposits, withdrawals, transfers, and electronic banking services, and to grant individual or joint signing powers as required. 5. IMPLEMENTATION. RESOLVED that the officers be and are authorized to complete all statutory registrations, including the New Zealand Business Number, Inland Revenue Department registration, GST, PAYE, and any applicable data protection or privacy registration, and to engage legal, accounting, and licensing advisers as required. Each resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Screening and Pre-Incorporation Constitutional Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Register), online name search and entity registration portal at companiesoffice.govt.nz.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a preliminary name search on the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm that NZ LIMITED or the operating business name is not identical or nearly identical to an existing company, reserved name, or registered trademark. Submit a draft application through the Companies Office online platform to validate company name availability. Prepare the constitutional and governance instruments: either adopt the default constitution set out in the Companies Act 1993 or file a bespoke constitution, and select the initial shareholder, directors, share quantum, and registered office. The name must not imply an activity prohibited in New Zealand and should accurately refer to a software or information technology business. For an ISIC 6201 SaaS analytics tool, the business description should refer to search engine data processing, web analytics, and content performance analysis. The applicant should also confirm that the registered office will be a physical street address, not a mail forwarding box.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and business description
Constitution instrument (if bespoke) or election to use the default constitution
Director name, date of birth, residential address, and written consent
Shareholder names and proposed share allotment
Registered office physical address and address for service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on similarity grounds, apply for a name reservation with the Companies Office or select a distinguishing suffix; if a third party files a formal objection, provide evidence of honest concurrent use or rebrand and refile under a revised name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Application for Registration and Payment of Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, electronic Companies Register, registry of the Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the New Zealand Companies Register and select register a company. Complete the application for registration under section 13 of the Companies Act 1993, entering company name, share structure, shareholder details, director details, registered office address, and address for service. Upload, where applicable, the signed consent forms of directors and the constitution. Review all statutory declarations and electronically attest truthfulness. Pay the official filing fee through the approved payment gateway. Submit the application and retain the transaction receipt. The Registrar will review the submission; where the application satisfies all statutory requirements, a certificate of incorporation is issued and an NZBN is allocated. Any deficiency is notified through the Register message centre.
required_dossiers: Completed online incorporation form
Director consent forms
Constitution if uploaded
Registered office consent of the occupant
Shareholder subscription details and share issue schedule
Payment confirmation receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries or suspends the application, respond through the Companies Register message centre within the specified evidentiary period, correct or supplement the required disclosures, and resubmit the application. Administrative review may be requested under the Companies Act 1993, and the Registrar may correct the register on application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation IRD Tax Registrations and NZBN Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD New Zealand) via myIR Secure Online Services and the New Zealand Business Registration Gateway.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the certificate of incorporation and NZBN, access the IRD business registration service. Apply for the company IRD number. Evaluate GST registration: if the value of taxable supplies exceeds NZ$60,000 in a 12-month period or is expected to exceed that threshold, GST must be registered immediately; for non-resident or offshore-facing SaaS, determine whether supplies are zero-rated under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 and whether reverse-charge rules apply. If employees are engaged in New Zealand, register as an employer for PAYE and employer superannuation where applicable. Notify local authorities of the registered office and, if physical premises are opened, advise the territorial authority for building compliance. Ensure all registrations align with the target payment rails.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN confirmation
Director and shareholder identification and tax details
IRD business registration form via myIR
GST registration election if applicable
PAYE employer registration information if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD application is placed in abeyance, log into myIR, verify the NZBN, update entity tax residence and expected New Zealand source income, and provide supporting explanation. Escalate through the IRD business relationship team and rely on review rights under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Onboarding and Statutory Registers Execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office for public register maintenance and annual return; Board of Directors for internal corporate governance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute and file minutes of the first board resolution and maintain a statutory register that records all share issues, director appointments, and registered office notifications. The Companies Office maintains the public register, but the company must keep its own share register and director register up to date. Issue share certificates to subscribers and obtain signed consent to act from each director. Set the accounting balance date and appoint an auditor or accountant where necessary under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, including early adoption of small-company reporting relief if eligible. If the company is non-resident-owned, review the Companies Office annual return filing requirement and the director register obligations. The first annual return must be filed before the first anniversary of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Executed First Board Resolution
Share Issue Ledger and share certificates
Director Register and written consents
Registered Office records and address for service details
Financial Reporting exemption election if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query regarding statutory records or annual return, file a corrective return online, apply for late filing remission if available, and ensure all director consents and registered office notices are on the public register before requesting expedited reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Authorization and Third-Party Payment Rail Integration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed New Zealand trading bank and third-party payment processors Stripe and Paddle; private-sector onboarding subject to AML/CFT supervision by the Department of Internal Affairs.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, use the executed board resolution to complete know-your-customer and client due diligence with a New Zealand licensed bank and with Stripe and Paddle. Provide the bank with a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation, NZBN confirmation, director and shareholder identification, proof of registered office, and IRD registration. The bank will perform AML/CFT screening; this SaaS entity is expected to be classified as a low-risk standard digital or software merchant. Complete the Stripe and Paddle merchant onboarding applications, including tax and payout details, and link the company bank account. Upon approval, issue the online banking credentials and authorized signatory list in accordance with the banking resolution.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN and IRD/GST registrations
Executed banking authorization resolution
Beneficial ownership and disclosure forms
Director and shareholder identity documents
Stripe and Paddle merchant onboarding questionnaires
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If banking onboarding is declined, request reconsideration with additional beneficial ownership evidence; appeal the merchant provider compliance decision and select an alternate licensed bank or payment processor having satisfied the same due diligence standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. New Zealand does not require an industrial or operating licence for digital software, SEO content analytics, data crawling, or consulting services under ISIC 6201.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable. No environmental protection agency jurisdiction is engaged for a pure digital and consulting activity under ISIC 6201.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. No Assessment of Environmental Effects or full environmental impact assessment is required under the Resource Management Act 1991 for the stated software analytics business.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. The business has zero industrial point-source wastewater discharges, zero VOC emissions, and zero hazardous waste handling. Any ordinary office waste must comply with territorial authority bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable. No Civil Defense fire permit, hazardous substance inventory, or industrial building warrant is triggered because the Company does not carry out physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing. If the Company later leases a physical office, the premises must comply with the Building Act 2004 and the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including general workplace fire safety, means of escape, and electrical safety obligations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand, operating through the myIR secure online portal (https://www.ird.govt.nz/). The New Zealand Companies Office (under the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment) handles company incorporation and issues the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), which is a prerequisite for most tax registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a New Zealand resident limited company (NZ_LTD), the following exhaustive procedure applies: (1) Incorporate the company with the New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Office / Āria) to obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) and Certificate of Incorporation. (2) Using the NZBN and company details, apply for a tax identification number known as the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) number. This can be completed online via myIR or by submitting form IR596 (Registration of a Company) to the IRD. Non-resident directors or shareholders must provide their foreign tax identification numbers, passports or national identity proofs, and overseas addresses as part of the application. (3) Upon successful processing, the IRD issues a unique 8 or 9-digit IRD number, which serves as the company's Tax File Number (TFN) for income tax and GST purposes. (4) While completing the registration, the company must also register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if its taxable turnover exceeded NZD 60,000 in the preceding 12 months or is expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in the next 12 months. If not immediately required, voluntary GST registration is available. (5) If the company will have employees or pay salaries, it must also register as an employer for PAYE (Pay As You Earn) and, if applicable, for FBT (Fringe Benefit Tax) and ACC (Accident Compensation Corporation) obligations. (6) The entire registration process is consolidated within myIR, and the IRD number is the single identifier used for all tax filings, including GST returns, income tax returns, and employer schedules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A New Zealand resident limited company is subject to corporate income tax on its worldwide income at the standard corporate rate of 28%. The default classification under New Zealand domestic law is entity-level taxation with no automatic pass-through treatment. Companies are entitled to imputation credits (dividend imputation) to avoid double taxation of distributed profits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not offer a US-style check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election under domestic law. However, an eligible closely-held New Zealand company (no more than 5 shareholders, none of which are companies, and meeting ownership tests) may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) status under the Income Tax Act 2007. If elected, the company's income, expenses, and tax credits are transparently attributed to shareholders, subject to eligibility criteria and a binding election filed with the IRD. LTC status is not available to non-resident companies or companies with corporate shareholders. Additionally, certain hybrid mismatch rules apply under the OECD BEPS framework, but these are not 'elections' but rather anti-avoidance provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (New Zealand).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000: A person or entity must register for GST if the total taxable supplies made in New Zealand (or intended to be made) exceeded NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, or if it is expected that the total value of taxable supplies will exceed NZD 60,000 in the next 12 months. Registration is also mandatory for non-resident persons who provide remote services (e.g., digital SaaS) to New Zealand consumers and exceed this threshold, but for a domestic NZ_LTD, the standard threshold rules apply. Voluntary registration is available even below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate a real-time fiscal clearance system, nor does it require anti-fraud digital stamping or government pre-approval of invoices. Electronic invoicing is permitted and encouraged, and the IRD supports the use of the Peppol network as a voluntary standard. There is no statutory API-based clearance mechanism for GST returns. However, all tax invoices must be retained in either paper or electronic form and contain prescribed information under the GST Act 1985, including: supplier name and GST number, date of issue, description of supply, consideration, and GST amount (or zero-rating statement for exports). For continuous supplies (e.g., SaaS subscriptions), a single tax invoice may cover recurring charges, but reconciliation records must be maintained.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, the supply of services is zero-rated if the services are supplied to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, and the services are not physically performed (directly in connection with) land or tangible personal property situated in New Zealand. For a SaaS-based SEO content analytics tool (ISIC 6201), zero-rating applies when the customer is a non-resident business or individual, the software/platform is used remotely, and the customer has no presence or nexus in New Zealand. The supplier must obtain and retain evidence of the customer's non-resident status and offshore consumption. Additionally, exports of goods are zero-rated when physically exported from New Zealand under customs supervision. Zero-rated GST does not entitle the supplier to a refund on input tax unless the input tax relates to taxable activities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial contract or service agreement with the non-resident customer, clearly stating the nature of the SaaS service, payment currency, and overseas jurisdiction.
Tax invoice issued under GST Act 1985 showing 0% GST, customer name and address outside New Zealand, and a zero-rating reference (e.g., Section 11(1)(m)).
Bank statement or SWIFT/remittance credit advice demonstrating payment from an overseas account (New Zealand banks do not issue FIRC; bank-generated settlement evidence is accepted).
IP address logs, server geolocation data, and customer self-certification (for B2B) or proof of customer's offshore address to substantiate non-resident consumption.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may subject zero-rated export claims to rigorous audit scrutiny, including verification of the customer's non-resident status, contractual terms, payment provenance, and the actual offshore consumption of the service. If zero-rating is claimed without adequate documentation, or is found to be fraudulent or misrepresented, the following penalties apply under the Tax Administration Act 1994: (a) shortfall penalties up to 20% or 40% for not taking reasonable care or gross carelessness, and 100% or 150% for fraudulent intent; (b) use-of-money interest from the original due date of GST; (c) retrospective GST assessments clawing back the unpaid GST plus interest and penalties, potentially extending to prior returns within the statutory reassessment period (typically 4 years, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud or suppression). In addition, criminal prosecution may be pursued for tax evasion offences, leading to fines up to NZD 50,000 for individuals and imprisonment up to 3 years. Directors and managers of the NZ_LTD may be held personally liable for penalties in cases of knowing participation in GST fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand does not maintain a stringent foreign exchange control regime. The New Zealand dollar is freely floating and fully convertible for both current account and capital account transactions. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand retains statutory powers to issue prudential and currency-related regulations, but it does not impose surrender requirements, prior approvals, or licensing hurdles on ordinary foreign exchange transactions. Inward capital contributions, equity injections, intra-group loans, royalty payments, and profit remittances may be converted into NZ dollars or foreign currency with minimal administrative friction. There is no statutory requirement to convert export proceeds into NZD, and no limitations on repatriating dividends, provided the usual corporate law solvency tests and tax clearance obligations are satisfied. Capital account openness is high, though certain overseas investments in sensitive land or significant business assets require consent under the Overseas Investment Act. For an ISIC 6201 software analytics company with no sensitive-asset exposure, convertibility is effectively unrestricted. Banks apply standard AML/CFT transaction monitoring and may request supporting documents for large cross-border flows, but there is no central bank foreign exchange approval gate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio exist for export foreign currency receipts. New Zealand resident exporters may retain receivables in foreign currency, hold NZD, or freely transact through any registered New Zealand bank, subject only to standard AML/CFT record-keeping and suspicious transaction reporting obligations.

Corporate NZD Business Account with SWIFT-linked USD/EUR sub-ledger
Corporate Transactional NZD Account plus Capital Escrow Sub-Account
Business NZD Account and Multi-Currency Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border digital EMI platforms are operationally viable in New Zealand for SaaS merchants but only under clear legal constraints. An EMI must either hold a New Zealand money remittance registration or operate as an appointed agent of a registered provider under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, with supervision by the Department of Internal Affairs. Such platforms are not licensed as registered banks and cannot provide insured deposit facilities; they may offer payment collection, FX conversion, and payout rails. A fintech EMI cannot replace the statutory corporate bank account required for audit trails, capital verification, and trade finance documentation. It is best positioned as a secondary ancillary rail for subscription collections and contractor payouts, while the primary treasury architecture remains anchored at a Tier 1 domestic bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand Tier 1 banks generally require at least one New Zealand-resident director or an authorized signatory to complete an in-person or live video identity verification interview. A fully remote consular proxy opening is not commonly accepted for a newly formed non-resident-owned company. Directors may use New Zealand-registered professional identity verification services, including Justice of the Peace certification, but the bank compliance committee will mandate original or certified documents such as signed board resolutions, passport pages, and proof of residential address. If no director is physically present in New Zealand, the onboarding process will likely require a targeted visit or the appointment of a New Zealand-based director or authorized representative with verified identity credentials.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain contains foreign nominee shareholders or trust structures without transparent disclosure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the New Zealand Companies Office register extract showing full shareholder lineage, executed shareholder registers, a copy of any trust deed or deed of settlement, a trust breakdown chart of settlor/appointor/trustee/beneficiary classes, and signed UBO declarations from all natural persons holding at least 25 percent of the entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial share capital injection originates from a non-NZD jurisdiction and may trigger source-of-funds concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit six months of bank statements from the remitting account, audited or certified annual financial statements of the overseas parent, executed capital contribution resolution, bank-generated SWIFT confirmation showing the true remitter, and a certified foreign-source-of-wealth statement covering the capital amount.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity SaaS subscription revenue creates a complex transaction footprint that may raise unlicensed money-service activity flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the executed SaaS master subscription agreement, platform payment scheme configuration showing collection via licensed payment facilitators, abandoned-cart and refund policy documents, a breakdown of recurring billing volumes, and a legal opinion confirming the business does not accept unlicensed deposits or perform payment processing beyond its software analytics scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or beneficial owners were included in sanctions or politically exposed person screening watchlists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certified passport copies, current visa or residence documentation, independent sanctions screening results from a recognized commercial provider, a clear off-shelf list match explanation if applicable, signed PEP declarations, and a detailed narrative source-of-wealth and source-of-funds profile approved by a supervisor or senior accountant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections should be routed through the SWIFT network using MT103 messages into the New Zealand company's NZD or foreign-currency account at a Tier 1 bank. The remitter must use a precise payment purpose description such as 'Equity subscription toward ordinary shares under the Companies Act 1993' and include appropriate ISO 20022 purpose code, generally 'PDBA' or the bank-designated code for foreign direct investment. No New Zealand Exchange Control approval is required, but the bank may request a board resolution, subscription agreement, and share allotment filing with the Companies Office. A New Zealand Chartered Accountant can issue a capital verification certificate, confirming the receipt and allocation of funds, which is particularly useful for future dividend distributions and capital repatriation documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements and SaaS vendor payments should use SWIFT MT103 for larger international wire transfers, with beneficiary bank and intermediary bank codes clearly specified. Commercial Letters of Credit issued by a Tier 1 New Zealand bank are appropriate for high-value procurement of hardware, cloud infrastructure, and licensed software development services requiring documentary risk mitigation. Documentary collections are viable for medium-value transactions where the New Zealand company and offshore supplier maintain established trade history. Subscription receipts from Stripe and Paddle should be settled into the merchant settlement account with automated daily sweeps to the primary NZD operating account, then converted into USD/EUR only as needed using the bank's spot or forward desk to avoid excessive conversion spreads.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts with licensed New Zealand bank counterparties
Foreign currency options executed under ISDA or local master trading agreements
Cross-currency swaps for long-term USD/NZD or EUR/NZD treasury exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible but generally redundant for New Zealand dollar exposure because the NZD is freely deliverable; NDFs may be used only for exotic or index-linked hedge structures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return to the New Zealand Companies Register (fee NZD 47.40, approximately USD 30.00)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than one calendar month after the annual return date, being the anniversary of incorporation; e.g. incorporation on 23 September requires filing by 22 October each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the Annual Return is not filed by the statutory date, the Registrar issues a reminder and then a notice of proposed removal after continued default; the company may be struck off the New Zealand Register during the ensuing 20-working-day objection period, causing dissolution and transfer of residual assets to the Crown; regulatory offence penalties for late or non-filing also apply under section 85 of the Companies Act 1993.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company income tax return (IR4), terminal tax payment, and provisional tax instalments for the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, IR4 return filing is due by 7 July following balance date unless an IRD-approved tax agent extension applies; provisional tax instalments are due 28 August, 15 January and 7 May; terminal tax is due by 7 February following the tax year. Non-standard balance dates use the corresponding month-shifted IRD dates.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 50 per month of lateness up to a maximum of NZD 500; late payment penalty of 1% of the unpaid amount imposed immediately plus 1% for each further month or part-month; use-of-money interest (UOMI) accrues at the IRD published underpayment rate; enforcement remedies include compulsory deduction notices and debt recovery action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Goods and services tax (GST) return and payment (IR372) for each GST taxable period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly taxable periods end on 31 March, 30 June, 30 September and 31 December; returns and payments are due by the 28th day of the month following each period, i.e. 28 April, 28 July, 28 October and 28 January respectively. Monthly filers must file and pay by the 28th day of the following month; GST registration is compulsory once annual taxable supplies reach NZD 60,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 50 per month late up to a maximum of NZD 500; late payment penalty of 1% of the unpaid amount immediately plus 1% per month or part-month thereafter; UOMI applies to overdue GST; persistent non-compliance may result in IRD assessment, collection action, and enforcement without prior notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Fringe benefit tax (FBT) return and payment (IR422) where the company provides fringe benefits to employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March tax year and an annual filing election, the annual FBT return and full payment are due by 20 April following the end of the tax year; quarterly filers must follow IRD quarter-end dates with payment due by the 20th day of the month after each quarter close.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 50 per month late capped at NZD 500; late payment penalty of 1% immediately and 1% monthly thereafter; UOMI is imposed on outstanding FBT; IRD may require voluntary disclosure and can assess penalties for inaccurate filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial statements package delivered to the Companies Register where the company is large, an FMC reporting entity, or otherwise required to file audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be prepared within 5 months of balance date; where an audit is required, the audit must be completed within 4 months of balance date; the signed financial statements must be delivered to the Companies Office within 20 working days after they are issued to shareholders. For a 31 March balance date, practical delivery is therefore around late August to early September.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to deliver financial statements commit an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Companies Act 1993; the Registrar may seek Court compliance orders; directors may be liable for fines and the company may be subject to continuing registration penalties including eventual removal from the Companies Register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Companies Act 1993, Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, an independent certified statutory audit is compulsory if any one of the following quantitative or qualitative thresholds is met for either of the two preceding accounting periods: (i) total assets equal or exceed NZD 60 million (approximately USD 36 million); (ii) total annual turnover or revenue equals or exceeds NZD 30 million (approximately USD 18 million); (iii) the company employs 50 or more full-time-equivalent employees; (iv) the company is an FMC reporting entity; (v) the company is a subsidiary of a large company or overseas parent and does not qualify for an exemption; or (vi) the shareholders by special resolution or the company constitution require an independent audit. Any audit must be performed by a licensed auditor authorised under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and in accordance with International Standards on Auditing (New Zealand).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For-profit entities must apply the External Reporting Board (XRB) accounting standards framework: large entities and publicly accountable entities apply New Zealand equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS); eligible Tier 2 entities apply NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR); non-reporting companies must still maintain accounting records and prepare financial statements satisfying section 194 of the Companies Act 1993.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not operate a separate annual UBO confirmation return. The annual return to the Companies Office operates as the annual statutory confirmation of shareholder and officer details. Any change of directors, shareholders, registered office or constitution must be notified to the Companies Office within 20 working days of the change. Internally, a transfer of shares must be entered in the Register of Members within 30 days of the date of transfer, with the company remaining responsible for the accuracy and completeness of its share and director registers.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges (Mortgages and Charges over Company Assets)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150.00 - USD 600.00 per annum depending on the registered office, company secretarial and share registry agent selected; the standard New Zealand corporate service provider market falls within this range.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000.00 - USD 25,000.00 per annual audit cycle for a low-risk MarTech/SaaS company with a certified New Zealand audit firm; actual fees vary with group structure, consolidation, transaction testing and disclosure scope.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Full deduction for R&D expenditure, plus a 15% R&D Tax Credit on eligible third-party R&D spend. Immediate deduction for low-cost assets (NZ$5,000 or less). A 20% depreciation loading is available on fixed-life assets in certain industries. Losses are deductible indefinitely subject to ownership continuity or business continuity rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (subject to 49% same-owner continuity for 5-year-old losses, or business continuity test after ownership breach; no absolute year cap)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically via myIR (Inland Revenue online portal) or IRD-approved tax software (e-file/e-File).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be filed by 7 July (i.e., the 7th day of the 4th month following balance date). A registered tax agent may obtain an automatic filing extension to 7 April of the following year. Provisional tax is payable in three instalments – 28 August, 15 January and 7 May (for 31 March balance dates).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare all gross income derived by the company during the year, including business income, interest, dividends, rents, royalties and government grants. Exempt and non-assessable income must be separately scheduled.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A New Zealand resident company owned by non-residents must report all assessable New Zealand-sourced income and any foreign-sourced income derived by the company. Foreign dividends and branch profits require disclosure in supplementary schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim deductible expenses incurred in deriving assessable income, such as wages, rent, interest, depreciation, software development costs, marketing, legal and professional fees. Expenses must be supported by invoices or equivalent evidence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses wholly or partly incurred in deriving assessable income are deductible. Cross-border payments to related non-resident entities (e.g., management fees, royalties, interest) must satisfy the arm's length principle under transfer pricing rules and be supported by substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income equals Box 1 minus Box 2. If negative, the result is a tax loss. Tax losses may be carried forward to subsequent years subject to continuity rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A loss arising in a NZ company is available for carry-forward only if the company meets the shareholder continuity rule (49% or more of that loss component remains held by the same persons) or, after an ownership breach, the business continuity test is satisfied. Losses from foreign-sourced income are subject to additional anti-treaty shopping rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the basic corporate income tax at the statutory rate of 28% on Box 3 (net taxable income). The result is the headline tax liability, before crediting R&D tax credits, foreign tax credits and provisional tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 28% rate applies uniformly to all resident NZ companies, irrespective of the residency of shareholders. Non-resident-owned companies do not receive a reduced rate under domestic law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the balance of the imputation credit account and the net imputation credits attached to dividends paid during the year. This reconciliation is mandatory for every company paying dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When paying dividends to non-resident shareholders, the company must attach imputation credits in accordance with applicable rules. Imputation credits can affect the NRWT rate and treaty relief. The shareholder must provide the payer with Form IR8 and a Tax Residency Certificate to claim treaty benefits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR4 incurs a late filing penalty (LFP) of NZ$50 immediately, with a further NZ$50 for each month the return remains outstanding, capped at NZ$500. In addition, late payment of terminal tax attracts a late payment penalty (LPP) of 1% of the unpaid tax per month or part-month. If the understatement is attributable to careless or intentional behaviour, shortfall penalties of 20% to 150% of the tax shortfall can be imposed. A company that fails to file after a reminder notice may be exposed to civil penalties of up to NZ$1,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The statutory Non-resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) rate on dividends is 30%. This rate is reduced to 15% for a fully imputed dividend paid by a New Zealand resident company. Under certain DTAs, the rate may be further reduced – for instance, Australia grants a 5% rate on dividends where the beneficial owner holds at least 80% of the voting power. The US DTA generally allows 15% (5% for 10%-or-more shareholdings).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a lower DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder (beneficial owner) must provide the New Zealand company with a completed Form IR8 – Certificate of Exemption from NRWT – before the dividend is paid. The Form IR8 must be accompanied by a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's country of residence. The NZ payer is responsible for verifying and retaining the certificate to apply the treaty rate at source. If the certificate is not received before payment, the statutory 30% (or 15% for fully imputed dividends) must be withheld and the shareholder may seek a refund through the IRD on a case-by-case basis. For interest, an Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) at 2% can eliminate the 15% NRWT if the payer is an approved issuer and the loan is an 'approved instrument'.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on interest is 15%. Statutory NRWT on royalties is 15%. These rates are frequently reduced under New Zealand's DTAs – e.g., US: interest 10%, royalties 10%; Australia: interest 10%, royalties 5% for industrial royalties; Japan: interest 10%, royalties 10%. A tax agent or payer must obtain a valid TRC and Form IR8 before applying the treaty rate. Without the correct documentation, the statutory rate will be withheld.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A New Zealand company with cross-border transactions with associated non-resident enterprises must prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File) when the aggregate gross value of all such transactions exceeds NZ$10 million in an income year. A Master File is required for multinational groups where the ultimate parent's annual consolidated group revenue exceeds NZ$1.2 billion. Even below these thresholds, taxpayers are expected to retain reasonable supporting documentation to demonstrate an arm's length outcome.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand has no standalone 'Economic Substance Regulations' (ESR) as applied in certain offshore financial centres. However, the Inland Revenue Act 2007, specifically s GA 1 (general anti-avoidance rule), the business continuity test for losses, and the underlying purpose of the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and DTAs require that a NZ company demonstrate genuine commercial substance. Maintaining an office, having local staff, holding board meetings in NZ, executing key contracts locally, and exercising real decision-making functions are essential. A shell company or 'letterbox' arrangement without substance will be disregarded for tax purposes, its transactions re-characterised, and penalties imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating global business income, fabricating invoices, destroying relevant accounting records, or diverting profits to an undisclosed offshore bank account for the purpose of avoiding New Zealand corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under s 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994, carrying a maximum fine of NZ$50,000 per offence on the company. The company may be liable for a shortfall penalty of 150% of the avoided tax, plus late payment penalties and interest. Under s 144, aiding and abetting tax evasion attracts the same penalties. Criminal conviction may result in confiscation of proceeds under the Proceeds of Crime Act 1994.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who are knowingly concerned in the evasion can be held personally liable for the company's tax shortfall under s 149 of the Tax Administration Act. They may face a separate criminal fine of up to NZ$50,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years under the Crimes Act 1961. Travel bans and asset freezing orders can be imposed under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a nominally registered New Zealand company that lacks real business premises, employees, and local management, while directing all significant operational decisions from abroad. The company invoices onshore clients for service fees but provides no substantive value added in New Zealand, enabling profit shifting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner of Inland Revenue may invoke the general anti-avoidance rule (s BG 1, s GA 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007) to disregard the company as a taxpayer or reallocate income to the true source. The company will lose the benefit of any tax deductions, face reassessment of income at 28% with interest, and be liable for shortfall penalties of 40% (gross negligence) or 100% (abusive tax position) of the resulting tax shortfall. The company's loss carry-forward may be denied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorised or participated in the formation and operation of such a shell arrangement may be personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax under s 149 of the Tax Administration Act. Additionally, they may be charged with tax evasion under s 143A causing a travel ban, and may be barred from managing a company for up to 5 years under the Companies Act 1993.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in cross-border related-party transactions with an associated overseas entity at prices that deviate from the arm's length principle, e.g., paying highly inflated royalties for intellectual property to a low-tax jurisdiction, or charging artificially low management fees to a related enterprise, and failing to document the pricing rationale.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may make a transfer pricing adjustment under Part GC (s GC 6 and GC 7) of the Income Tax Act 2007, increasing the company's taxable income by the offending margin, plus interest. Shortfall penalties of up to 100% of the additional tax can be applied, and up to 150% in the case of intentional disregard of the rules. The company's ability to claim a penalty reduction is lost if contemporaneous documentation is absent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for setting transfer prices without commercial justification and without attempting to comply with the arm's length principle may be held personally liable for the associated shortfall penalties under s 141CB of the Tax Administration Act. In egregious cases, directors may be prosecuted for tax evasion, leading to imprisonment and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to implement an AML/CFT compliance programme required under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act) when providing financial services or as a 'reporting entity', failing to conduct customer due diligence (CDD) on non-resident owners or users of the SEO content analytics platform, or failing to report a suspicious transaction involving proceeds of tax evasion or bribery.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the AML/CFT Act, a company that is a reporting entity can be fined up to NZ$100,000 for non-compliance, and directors may be fined up to NZ$50,000. In serious cases, civil penalties may reach NZ$200,000 per contravention. The AML/CFT supervisor (the Department of Internal Affairs or the Financial Markets Authority) may also issue compliance orders, suspend or cancel registration, and the company may be added to the public warning list.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who were knowingly involved in the AML/CFT breach can be personally fined up to NZ$50,000 under s 110 of the AML/CFT Act. For deliberate money laundering, directors face prosecution under the Crimes Act 1961 with up to 7 years' imprisonment, and under s 9E of the AML/CFT Act may receive up to 2 years' imprisonment for obstruction. Travel bans may be imposed as a condition of bail or sentence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Taking an overly aggressive interpretation of the tax law in a tax return that is not 'more likely than not' to be correct, e.g., claiming tax-deductible management fees for services not actually provided to the company, or claiming R&D tax credits for activities that are not eligible under the R&D criteria.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue will reassess the tax shortfall and impose shortfall penalties: 20% for an 'unacceptable tax position' (if the tax shortfall exceeds the threshold of NZ$10,000 or 1% of gross income, whichever is greater), 40% for gross carelessness, and 100% for an abusive tax position. A further 20% penalty may apply if the taxpayer has a history of the same issue. Late payment interest accrues from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or directly participated in the preparation or lodgement of the return without reasonable care can be personally liable for the shortfall penalties under s 141CB. If the position is fraudulent, personal criminal liability attaches under s 143A with imprisonment possible.
